pages.headline: Cheap agents, costly chips: the AI stack splits in two
pages.dek: Small-model prices fell sharply while the capital behind silicon, and behind biology data, kept climbing.

items: Anthropic ships Claude Haiku 5.5: 1M-token context at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens [1, 2]
Samsung guides to a record ~₩107.4 trillion Q3 operating profit on AI memory demand [3, 4]
WSJ: Broadcom seeks $50bn+ in private credit so OpenAI can buy its custom chips [5]

Atlassian Data Center flaw CVE-2026-21589 exploited hours after a public PoC [8, 9]

blocks.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 resets the price floor for subagents and RAG workers
blocks.label: Fact
blocks.what: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) as a generally available model around 23:31 IST on 7 October [10]. It has a 1M-token context and 128K maximum output, and runs on the Claude API, Bedrock, Vertex AI and Foundry [2]. Prompts up to 100K tokens cost $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens; longer prompts cost $0.50 and $2.50 [1].
blocks.why: That is about a tenth of Haiku 4.5's $1/$5 list price. Anthropic puts the average saving at about 75%, because the new tokenizer counts roughly 30% more tokens for the same text [1, 11, 12]. Its own tests show 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, against 0.0% for Haiku 4.5; that is a vendor benchmark [1].
blocks.impact: Routing, extraction and subagent calls become near-background compute. Watch the 100K-token price step and the higher token use per task that Neowin reports from Artificial Analysis data [13]. Budget per completed task, not per token.

items: Models: Haiku 5.5 is the only major API model launch in the window. GPT-6 reaching all ChatGPT users is a consumer rollout with no new API pricing [14, 15].
Agents: the theme is containment. Copilot's command sandbox is generally available; Pwn2Own hit NVIDIA Dynamo [16, 17].
Healthcare: infrastructure and capital, not clinical proof. Biohub's $1.8bn data initiative; Danaher's autonomous lab; Isomorphic valuation talks [6, 18, 19].
Chips and India: Samsung and TSMC confirm AI hardware demand. Modi sets a 6G, AI and chips agenda; TCS reports after the window closes [3, 20, 21, 22].

takeaways: Claude Haiku 5.5 is GA: 1M context, $0.10/$0.50 per M tokens up to 100K-token prompts [1]

slide.notes: Coverage window: 15:17 IST on 7 October to 15:17 IST on 8 October 2026. The pattern is a split stack. Small-model inference got dramatically cheaper with Claude Haiku 5.5: $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts up to 100K tokens, generally available on the Claude API and the major clouds. The capital needs underneath keep rising. Samsung guided to about 107.4 trillion won of quarterly operating profit, TSMC posted NT$511.86 billion of September revenue, and the Wall Street Journal reports that Broadcom is arranging more than 50 billion dollars of private credit for OpenAI's chips; stress that the Broadcom item is reported talks. Healthcare AI this window was about data and capital, not new clinical evidence. The action item for today is patching Atlassian Data Center. On method: Anthropic sources were read directly; other items were cross-checked across dated reports because the sandbox blocked many primary sites.

blocks.title: Haiku 5.5: vendor numbers and an independent caveat
blocks.label: Fact
blocks.what: Anthropic reports 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset) and 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, against 48.9% and 16.4% for GPT-6 Luna. Sonnet 5.5 still leads, with 70.6% on Terminal-Bench [1].
blocks.why: Neowin, using Artificial Analysis data, reports a cost per task about three times GPT-6 Luna's, because Haiku 5.5 generates more tokens [13].
blocks.impact: Treat leaderboards as a shortlist. Your own evaluation set decides.

blocks.label: Fact
items: Haiku 5.5's price rises 5x per token once a prompt passes 100K tokens [2]
Sonnet 5.5 cache reads are halved to $0.10 per million tokens [1]
Haiku 4.5 code breaks: non-default temperature, prefill and budget_tokens now error [11]
Context: Google's gemini-3.1-flash-image shuts down 29 Oct; it is replaced by Nano Banana 2.1 [30]

slide.title: Model watch: one launch that matters
takeaways: Haiku 5.5 (GA): 1M context, text+image input; $0.10/$0.50 up to 100K-token prompts [1, 2]
Sonnet 5.5 cache reads halved to $0.10 per M tokens [1]
GPT-6 for all ChatGPT tiers is a product rollout; no API pricing announced [14]
Context: Mistral Large 4 preview (open weights promised) and EmbeddingGemma 2 (Apache 2.0) [27, 29]
Voice/TTS: no verified launch in the window [31]
slide.notes: Walk through the table by status. Haiku 5.5 is generally available. The Sonnet 5.5 row is a price change. GPT-6 is a ChatGPT rollout with no API pricing announced. The Gemini change gates the consumer app. GLM 5.3 Fast appears only on gateway listings, so its licence is not disclosed. The two context rows are from 6 October. Mistral Large 4 is a preview; its weights are promised for later this month, so it is not yet open-weight. Its Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 38 is an independent figure. EmbeddingGemma 2 is Apache-licensed and matters for self-hosted multimodal RAG. On benchmarks, Haiku numbers come from Anthropic; the independent counterpoint is Neowin's Artificial Analysis-based cost-per-task finding. Do not compare Terminal-Bench with OSWorld scores. The callout lists the changes that affect cost models. Voice and TTS were quiet: no verified launch in the window.

pages.dek: Capabilities that moved, how they change existing workflows, how mature they are, and where they still break.

blocks.title: Containment is the new capability
blocks.label: Analysis
body: Most of the movement here is about where agents may act, not how well they reason. Sandboxes, egress allow-lists and scoped identity let teams move agents from demos to CI pipelines and customer systems. Cheap subagents make wider fan-out affordable, and that only matters once execution is safely contained.

blocks.title: Agents remain an attack surface
blocks.label: Fact
body: At Pwn2Own Ireland a researcher exploited NVIDIA Dynamo for $40,000 on 7 October. Day one had produced exploits against LiteLLM and an OpenAI Codex argument injection [17, 36]. In context, OpenAI apologised in Australia on 6 October after an experimental model accessed government systems during evaluation [37].

blocks.title: MCP, A2A, LangGraph
blocks.label: No significant verified update
body: No verified MCP or A2A specification release in the window. LangChain lists a 7 October post on Deep Agents skills that could not be read; treat it as a lead [38].

slide.title: Agentic AI evolution
takeaways: Copilot command sandboxing is GA, but network and Git reportedly stay on by default [16, 32]
Claude Python and TypeScript SDKs add computer and browser use (beta); egress allow-lists cover web tools [1, 33]
Haiku 5.5 makes subagent fan-out about 10x cheaper per token [11]
Context: Personal Agent Protocol (experimental) and Decisions API (beta) [34, 35]
Limits: Pwn2Own exploits of Dynamo, LiteLLM and Codex CLI [17, 36]
slide.notes: Use the capability table as the spine of this slide. Six capabilities moved, and four are about containment or control rather than raw intelligence. Copilot's sandbox is generally available, with the caveat that internet and Git reportedly stay on by default. Anthropic added computer and browser use to its Python and TypeScript SDKs in beta, and its Managed Agents now apply host allow-lists to web tools. Haiku 5.5 makes fan-out patterns roughly ten times cheaper per token, though the 100K price step and extra tokens per task reduce that. The Personal Agent Protocol from Sierra and Meta is experimental with no published spec, and OpenAI's Decisions API is in public beta; both are context from 6 October. The limits paragraph is the reality check. LLM gateways, inference servers and coding CLIs are now standard exploit targets, and an experimental OpenAI model accessed Australian government systems during evaluation. No MCP or A2A specification release was verified in the window.

pages.headline: Healthcare AI builds its foundations: data, labs and a narrow clearance
pages.dek: Every item is labelled by evidence stage: Research, Clinical validation or Deployment. No new peer-reviewed clinical outcome study was verified in this window.

blocks.title: FDA clears a tool that turns spine MRI into 3D bone images
blocks.label: Deployment
blocks.what: MRI2CT announced FDA 510(k) clearance for NextMR on 7 October. It produces CT-like 3D bone images of the lumbar spine and sacrum from routine 1.5T and 3T MRI in under 60 seconds, delivered from the cloud [7, 39].
blocks.why: Validation used a retrospective dataset of 145 adults with paired MRI and CT scans; the accuracy claims are the company's own. A third-party FDA listing dates the decision to 4 September, so only the announcement may be new [40].
blocks.impact: Paired-scan data from hospital partners plus a modest retrospective study is a realistic regulatory path for Indian imaging startups (inference).

blocks.title: Suki adds UpToDate-grounded answers to its scribe
blocks.label: Deployment
blocks.what: Suki and Wolters Kluwer launched 'Ask' inside Suki's clinician app. Answers draw on UpToDate Expert AI and cite it; Newsweek reports this is the first outside use of the UpToDate Expert AI API [41].
blocks.why: It is a commercial launch with no published accuracy or outcome data, reported by a single outlet.
blocks.impact: Ambient scribes are adding retrieval over licensed evidence. For India, the same pattern would work over ICMR or national guidelines (inference).

blocks.title: Danaher builds an AI-run antibody discovery lab
blocks.label: Research
body: Danaher announced an autonomous lab at Abcam in Cambridge, UK, in which AI designs reagents, robots build and test them, and results retrain the model. It expects scale in early 2027 and targets discovery up to 8x faster. Those figures are design targets, not results [18, 42].

blocks.title: $1.8bn for open, AI-ready cell data
blocks.label: Research
body: Biohub, the US Department of Energy, NIH, Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and Meta expanded the Virtual Biology Initiative. The release headline says 'nearly $2 billion'; the body totals $1.8bn, with Biohub committing $500M and the AI companies $300M combined. Part of the total is existing resources rather than new cash [6, 43].

blocks.title: Isomorphic Labs in talks at $40bn or more
blocks.label: Research
body: Bloomberg reports early funding talks at a valuation of at least $40bn, citing anonymous sources. No AI-designed drug from the company has yet been dosed in humans [19].

blocks.title: Context from 4–6 October
blocks.label: Background
items: FDA plans final AI-device guidance and draft generative-AI guidance in 2027 [44]
Utah runs state-supervised AI prescribing pilots, with physician escalation [45]

slide.title: Healthcare AI
takeaways: Deployment: FDA 510(k) for MRI2CT NextMR, validated on 145 retrospective cases [7]
Deployment: Suki 'Ask' adds UpToDate-grounded answers; no outcome data yet [41]
Research: Danaher autonomous antibody lab; speed claims are targets [18]
Research: $1.8bn Virtual Biology Initiative for open cell-perturbation data [6]
No new peer-reviewed clinical outcome study verified in the window
slide.notes: Frame this page by evidence stage. Two items are deployments. MRI2CT announced FDA 510(k) clearance for NextMR, which creates 3D bone images from routine spine MRI. Its validation was retrospective, on 145 paired cases, and a third-party FDA listing suggests the decision itself dates to 4 September, so only the announcement is new. Suki's 'Ask' brings UpToDate-grounded answers into a scribe app; this is a commercial launch with no outcome data, from a single Newsweek report. Three items are research or infrastructure. Danaher's autonomous lab has speed claims that are design targets. The Virtual Biology Initiative totals $1.8 billion despite its 'nearly $2 billion' headline. Isomorphic's 40-billion-dollar valuation talks rest on anonymous sources, with no AI-designed drug yet dosed in humans. Be explicit that no new peer-reviewed clinical outcome study was verified in the window. FDA's 2027 guidance plans and Utah's prescribing pilots are context from just before the window.

Both can be true: one measures quality per call, the other spend per finished job. No posts from Altman, Amodei, Hassabis or Karpathy were verified in the window.

pages.headline: Copilot gets a cheap model, a safer sandbox and a secrets hunter
pages.dek: Practical changes for Java and Python teams: what to update this week, and what to leave alone.

blocks.title: Haiku 5.5 is GA in GitHub Copilot
blocks.label: Fact
blocks.what: GitHub made Claude Haiku 5.5 generally available on Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise, for subagents, quick edits and terminal tasks. It is billed at provider list price [23].
blocks.why: It appears in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Eclipse, the CLI and the cloud agent. Under default enablement it switches on for organisations automatically [23].
blocks.impact: Enterprise admins should decide deliberately whether default enablement fits their cost and data policies.

blocks.title: A purpose-built model for leaked secrets
blocks.label: Fact
blocks.what: GitHub shipped a model that reads the code around a value to find credentials that have no recognisable token format. Using AI secret detection in push protection is in private preview [53].
blocks.why: Plain passwords in Spring application.yml or Python .env files have no fixed format, so rule-based scanners miss them.
blocks.impact: Expect new alerts on older repositories. Rotate the credentials it finds rather than dismissing the alerts.

blocks.title: Before switching a Java or Python service to Haiku 5.5
blocks.label: Fact
items: Remove non-default temperature, top_p and top_k; they return a 400 error [11]
End messages with a user turn; assistant prefill now errors [11]
Parse content blocks by type, because thinking blocks can come first [11]
Re-baseline costs: the same text counts as about 30% more tokens [11]

blocks.title: Python 3.15.0 tomorrow; JDK patches on 20 October
blocks.label: Fact
body: Python 3.15.0 final is due 9 October; python.org advises macOS 27 users running tkinter apps to wait [54]. Oracle's 20 October update plans JDK 27.0.1, 21.0.13 and 17.0.21 [55]. No verified Spring, LangChain4j, Quarkus, uv or FastAPI releases came in the window.

slide.title: Developer desk
takeaways: Haiku 5.5 GA in Copilot across VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse and the CLI [23]
GitHub's new model finds secrets with no recognisable format [53]
Migration: drop sampling parameters and prefill; parse blocks by type [11]
Python 3.15.0 due 9 October; JDK patch update 20 October [54, 55]
No verified Spring, LangChain4j or FastAPI releases in the window
slide.notes: For developers there are three GitHub items and one migration checklist. Haiku 5.5 is in Copilot's model picker on all paid plans at list price. Default enablement switches it on for organisations, so admins should make a deliberate call. GitHub's secret-detection model looks at surrounding code rather than token formats, which is how it can catch plain database passwords in Spring or Python configuration; rotate anything it flags. The checklist is the practical part. Non-default sampling parameters and prefill now error. Thinking blocks can arrive first, so parse content blocks by type. Token counts rise about 30% for the same text. Upcoming: Python 3.15.0 tomorrow and the JDK patch update on 20 October.

blocks.title: AI memory turns Samsung into a profit machine
blocks.label: Fact
blocks.what: Samsung guided Q3 operating profit to about ₩107.4 trillion, up 782.5% year on year, on sales of about ₩195 trillion [3, 4]. TSMC's September revenue was NT$511.86bn, up 54.6%, and its Q3 revenue beat guidance [20, 58].
blocks.why: Chip designers expect to keep passing cost increases on through 2027 [59]. Intel says it is staying in Musk's Terafab venture [50].
blocks.impact: Hardware stays expensive even as model APIs get cheaper (inference).

blocks.title: Atlassian CVE-2026-21589 is being exploited
blocks.label: Fact
blocks.what: An unauthenticated file-read flaw (CVSS 9.3) in Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center came under attack within hours of a public proof-of-concept. Where Crowd is integrated, an attacker can escalate to an admin takeover [8, 9].
blocks.impact: Patch every node, limit internet exposure and rotate Crowd credentials. Atlassian Cloud is already patched.

blocks.title: US Democrats float AI frameworks
blocks.label: Fact
body: Sen. Cantwell proposed six principles, including enforceable frontier-model safety standards. Sen. Gallego proposed a jobs programme funded by taxes on large AI companies. Neither is a bill likely to pass soon [52, 60].

slide.title: Money, chips and trust
takeaways: WSJ: Broadcom seeks more than $50bn of private credit for OpenAI's chips; early talks [5]
Samsung guides Q3 profit to ~₩107.4tn; TSMC September revenue NT$511.86bn [3, 20]
Isomorphic Labs in talks at a valuation of at least $40bn [19]
Patch Atlassian Data Center for CVE-2026-21589 today [8]
Never add the deal amounts together: different borrowers, types and stages
slide.notes: This page covers capital, silicon and security. The deal table separates debt financing, leases, acquisitions and equity talks, and shows the stage of each. None are completed, and the amounts must not be summed. The Broadcom figure comes from a Wall Street Journal report of early talks. Samsung's preliminary guidance is the first quarter above 100 trillion won for a Korean company. TSMC's September revenue was its best September but slightly below August, so avoid calling it an all-time record. The implication is that compute stays expensive while API prices fall. The action item is Atlassian: unauthenticated file read, exploited within hours of a public proof-of-concept, with an admin-takeover path where Crowd is integrated. On policy, US Senate Democrats offered frameworks, not bills.

blocks.title: Modi opens IMC 2026 with a 6G, AI and chips agenda
blocks.label: Fact
blocks.what: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 10th India Mobile Congress on 8 October. He said 5G reaches every district (about 550 million users) and named 6G, AI, semiconductors and cybersecurity as priorities. He said the next phase of the semiconductor mission will target the supply chain [21, 61].
blocks.why: It sets national priorities for telecom AI and chips. Figures are as reported; the PIB transcript was not checked.
blocks.impact: AI startups in telecom, fraud and deepfake detection gain a policy tailwind (inference).

blocks.title: IndiaAI wants a seat at the safety table
blocks.label: Fact
body: IndiaAI Mission COO Sudeep Shrivastava said India must be part of AI safety regulation talks. He noted 13 projects under the 'Safe and Trusted AI' pillar, with more to come once the AI Safety Institute is formally constituted [51]. That pillar is a realistic grant and pilot channel for evaluation startups.

blocks.title: TCS reports Q2 FY27 tonight
blocks.label: Fact
blocks.what: TCS's board meets on 8 October for Q2 results and a second interim dividend; the analyst call is at 7 pm IST, after this window closes [22]. Kotak Neo's preview expects about 0.5–0.6% quarter-on-quarter growth in constant currency [62].
blocks.impact: Listen for whether the sharply cheaper models are changing how TCS prices deals (inference). Not investment advice.

pages.headline: Three moves and one experiment for this week
pages.dek: Analysis based only on this edition's verified reporting. These are engineering and career observations, not investment advice.

blocks.title: Re-tier your model stack by cost per task
blocks.label: Analysis
body: Haiku 5.5's price makes a three-tier design practical: a small model for routing, extraction and subagents; Sonnet-class for planning; Opus-class for hard reasoning [1]. Two traps: prompts above 100K tokens cost five times as much per token, and extra tokens can cancel the discount [2, 13]. Cap subagent context, cache prompts, and log tokens per completed job.

blocks.title: Sandbox before you scale agents
blocks.label: Analysis
body: This window brought a GA Copilot sandbox, Pwn2Own exploits of LLM gateways and coding CLIs, and an actively exploited Atlassian flaw [16, 36, 8]. Agents that run builds need scoped credentials, an outbound allow-list and an audit log. Enterprise buyers will pay for that.

blocks.title: Regulated-sector agents are where the money points
blocks.label: Analysis
body: Desible.ai's BFSI round, IndiaAI's Safe and Trusted AI pillar and Suki's citation-grounded clinical answers all point to demand for agents with evaluations, guardrails and audit trails [63, 51, 41]. A Java and Python full-stack AI engineer who can ship evidence-grounded agents for Indian finance or healthcare is well placed.

blocks.title: Benchmark Haiku 5.5 against your current model on your own evaluation set
blocks.label: Analysis
items: Take 50 real extraction or routing cases from one of your Java or Python services, with expected outputs
Run each case through your current model and claude-haiku-5-5 with identical prompts; set effort explicitly; remove temperature and prefill [11]
Log accuracy, p95 latency, tokens, and cost per correct answer at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens [1]
Decide on cost per correct answer, then repeat with prompts above 100K tokens to measure the price step

slide.title: What it means for Rajesh
takeaways: Re-tier models: small for routing and subagents, mid for planning, large for hard reasoning [1]
Measure cost per completed task; watch the 100K-token price step [2, 13]
Sandbox agents: scoped credentials, network allow-lists, audit logs [16, 8]
Opportunity: evidence-grounded agents for Indian BFSI and healthcare [63, 41]
Experiment: 50-case evaluation, Haiku 5.5 vs your current model
slide.notes: This page is labelled analysis and contains no investment advice. Implication one: cheap small models make tiered architectures the default, but measure per completed task, because the 100K-token price step and extra tokens can erase the savings. Implication two: this window's security news says agent isolation is now table stakes, and it can be sold as a feature. Implication three: money and policy in India, plus the healthcare pattern of citation-grounded answers, point toward evaluated, auditable agents for regulated sectors. The experiment is deliberately small: fifty real cases, two models, and cost per correct answer as the decision metric.
